title: Entitlement-based security crediting & auto-evidence assembler pilot
creator: Liam Zhang
description: Pilot a new entitlement-driven model that grants customers security-evidence credits tied to contract tiers and automates assembly of CAIQ/SIG answers from verified artifacts. Goal is to reduce manual effort for customers and SEs while preserving auditability and minimizing evidence collection time for enterprise onboarding.
background: Enterprise customers repeatedly ask for faster delivery of completed security questionnaires (SIG/CAIQ) as part of negotiation. Current process is manual: SEs pull docs, redact, and assemble answers which increases sales cycle time and support load. Previous experiments focused on bundling attestation packs; this pilot ties credits to contract entitlements and attempts to auto-assemble evidence to reduce touch.
goals: Reduce average time-to-deliver a completed CAIQ from 7 business days to <48 hours for qualified customers
Decrease SE manual hours per contract by 60% for customers in qualifying tiers
Measure conversion impact and support load change for pricing tiers with credited evidence bundles
scope_in: Entitlement mapping: map billing tiers to number of evidence credits (small/medium/large)
Auto-evidence assembler service that pulls vetted artifacts (INFRA runbooks, SOC reports, architecture diagrams) and composes draft CAIQ answers
Console UI: allow customers/Sales to redeem credits and request auto-assembled responses
Billing integration to apply credits and track usage
scope_out: Full legal signature workflows (we will include audit trail but not replace contract-signing)
On-prem/on-air-gapped auto-assembly — only for hosted or VPC-managed control plane
Automated redaction of customer-provided documents (out of scope for pilot)
acceptance_criteria: Entitlement table implemented and visible in Console for trial accounts and Enterprise signups
Auto-evidence assembler produces draft CAIQ answers for at least 70% of questions for curated templates
Audit trail created for each assembled answer with source links and redaction flags
Billing shows credit consumption events and can be reconciled against usage dashboard
proposed_solution: Implement a service that references a curated artifact registry (Confluence pages, signed reports in Drive, GitHub PRs with security changes). When a credit is redeemed, service selects matching artifacts by signal (label, file metadata), runs templated answer generation with guardrails, and stores a reviewable draft in Console. Provide review flow for SE/security to finalize answers. Wire credit deductions into billing as line items.
tradeoffs: Speed vs. accuracy: faster drafts may require Security/SE review before being customer-facing
Surface area: pulling artifacts raises scope for leakage; must restrict to vetted repositories and implement access controls
Effort distribution: initial up-front investment in artifact curation and mapping; long-term savings for SEs
security_feedback: Security asked for immutable audit trail and per-assembly hash; must integrate with KMS for signing of assembled packages
Legal requires explicit record of which artifact versions were used and TTL for evidence (recommended 12 months)
Data access must obey customer VPC controls — auto-assembly only for hosted/VPC-managed customers, not for air-gapped or customer-hosted control planes
